name: SARM PCT

lead: SARM PCT is the community term for a 'post-cycle therapy' phase after using selective androgen receptor modulators. Users take it because SARMs can lower the body's own testosterone, and the aim is to restore it so that muscle and training capacity built during the run are kept.

The practice is borrowed from anabolic-steroid culture. Forum members disagree on whether it is needed after SARMs; some argue the compounds are mild and others report prolonged low testosterone and sexual side effects after use.

paras: Discussions describe a phase after the active run in which users take anti-estrogen or testosterone-stimulating drugs, often bought online, and check blood tests. Details of agents and amounts are not given here.

SARMs are not approved by the FDA or EMA, and online products are often mislabelled. Trials report that SARMs can suppress gonadotropins and testosterone and raise liver enzymes. Forum posters describe low testosterone and erectile dysfunction lasting a year or more after use. Medical supervision and bloodwork are the conventional route for hormone concerns.

chain: Use SARMs, which can lower natural testosterone
angle.text: Users take post-cycle compounds hoping to keep the physique gained during a SARM run. The practice addresses side effects of the drugs themselves and is discussed in forums rather than backed by trials.

lead: SARM PCT refers to post-cycle therapy used after a course of selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs), the unapproved research compounds popular among people building muscle. The goal people state is to recover natural testosterone production and hold on to gains made during the run.[1][2]

Appearance-wise, the chain is: restored hormone levels, then retained training capacity and muscle, then a fuller physique that persists. The practice is borrowed from anabolic steroid culture, and members of T Nation forums debate whether SARMs justify it at all.[2][3]
SARMs were first developed from 1998 and no regulator has approved one for therapeutic use; trials report that they can reduce testosterone and gonadotropins in a dose- and compound-dependent way.[4]
infobox: Anti-estrogens and testosterone-stimulating agents (as discussed in forums)
Not approved by FDA or EMA (as of 2023)

paras: PCT is a term from bodybuilding. After a SARM run, community members describe taking agents intended to counter hormone suppression. Forum posters disagree: one in a thread on PCT argued that a compound adding muscle is anabolic whatever it is called, while another said they would always recommend PCT after a long run.[2][5]

Users report widely different recoveries. One T Nation post described a major recovery of androgen levels after a restart, with total testosterone of 32.3 nmol/L reported in an update.[1] Others describe erectile dysfunction and reduced libido lasting around two years after SARM cycles, and one described possible gynecomastia after years of use.[6][7]

Reviews state that SARMs can suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, lowering gonadotropins and testosterone, with enobosarm among the least suppressive; they can also raise liver enzymes, and case reports link recreational use to liver injury.[4] Neither FDA nor EMA had approved a SARM as of 2023, and many online products are mislabelled.[4]

No studies found on PCT specifically after SARM use. Trials of SARMs themselves, such as the enobosarm phase III trial, reported increased lean body mass without significant improvement in physical function.[4]

lore.intro: PCT after SARMs is debated on T Nation, with advice ranging from routine use to the view that it is unnecessary.[2][5]

claims.claim: PCT is needed after SARM use
